Unilateral qualifier only on swelling; pain in calf not constrained to the same leg; risk factors dropped.
No-injury branch (check skin, pregnancy, kidney dipstick, refer) not encoded; only management/routing, so low impact. Statin note not encoded.
Probable arthropathy fires on any single difficulty finding or joint sign including joint swelling from injury, so sprain and arthropathy co-fire.

summary: Box 1 is largely well encoded (fracture, DVT, acute and critical limb ischaemia as probable diagnoses feeding an Urgent priority). Most consequential weaknesses are approximate mapping of exertional muscle pain to intermittent claudication and identical sprain/strain rules that co-fire with each other and with joint problem, plus dropped DVT risk factors and the no-injury branch. SNOMED concept validity was not verified because the snomed tool errored on my calls.
